record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README only; source code and result-file contents were not read.
record.tranche_reason: Applies a weight-edit version of difference-in-means refusal-direction removal and reports behavioral benchmarks. This is not the original single-direction activation-ablation intervention.
record.gate_note: The README reports benchmark outcomes for the weight-edited model. It describes the refusal prompts as legitimate educational and creative prompts, not harmful requests. The summary key stats say 20/20 for baseline capability and refusal, while the detailed tables report 50/50; the detailed tables are recorded below.
record.test_reason: The repo applies abliteration (per-layer difference-in-means weight orthogonalization) to Gemma 4 31B-IT. It reports only its own pipeline's results on a 100-prompt suite. The refusal half uses prompts the authors call legitimate educational and creative requests, and the stock model already answered all 50 of them. The suite therefore cannot show whether the edit removes refusal, so it gives no test of V2 or any other version. The capability-preservation result describes the method's own performance.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README claims 'full guardrail removal', zero capability degradation, zero refusals and 16% faster generation on its 100-prompt suite. It also concedes the stock model already answers most prompts, and says abliteration removes 'residual' refusal directions for consistency.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the harmful-minus-harmless mean difference, but computes a separate direction for each of 60 layers and orthogonalizes selected weight matrices rather than projecting out a single direction at every activation position. It then quantizes the edited weights to 4-bit.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says Gemma-family models are particularly resilient to abliteration and describes using per-layer directions. No comparative result for alternative settings is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Capability prompts answered were unchanged at 50/50 between the stock and the weight-edited 4-bit model, judged by a regex classifier.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: This per-layer abliteration of Gemma 4 31B-IT preserved answer rates on a 50-prompt capability suite.

record.problems: The README reports only 50 capability and 50 refusal prompts, with no uncertainty estimates. Its refusal prompts are described as legitimate educational or creative requests, and the stock model already answers all of them, limiting evidence that the edit removes refusals. The README's key-stats summary gives baseline 20/20 figures while the detailed tables give 50/50.
record.rows_left_out: No detailed category rows were left out. The README's summary key stats (baseline 20/20) are not separately rowed because they conflict with the detailed benchmark tables (50/50).

untested.parts: Compliance on harmful requests (including the 256 harmful prompts used to build the directions) before versus after the edit was not reported; no non-ceiling refusal baseline.
No activation ablation or addition, no induced-refusal test, no harmful-request compliance.
Per-layer directions are used but not compared with single-direction or cone accounts.

missing.what: Contents of the abliterated and baseline results files, comparison.md, and the iterative and v3 optimization results; these may hold harmful-prompt refusal rates or alternative settings.
Generation speed 20.41 vs 23.67 tok/s and peak memory 18.7 vs 19.1 GB, stock vs abliterated.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict is given because the refusal measure is at ceiling for the stock model, so neither removal nor failure is shown. The headline 'full guardrail removal' is not backed by any reported harmful-prompt result. The classifier is regex-based, and a response counts as refused only if refusal phrases appear and answer signals are absent. The key-stats table (20/20) conflicts with the detailed tables (50/50), and the README's '10 refusal categories' lists only 9. This is a self-published repo with no peer review and no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test ablating one direction at every layer and position or adding it to induce refusal; it computes separate directions for 60 layers and edits weights. It also does not test compliance with harmful requests.
The reported refusal prompts are legitimate educational or creative prompts; the study does not measure compliance with harmful requests. It does not report results for other released models.
No jailbreak attack or training against ablation is evaluated.
No comparison of affine, cone, single-direction, or multi-direction accounts.
No separate measure of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or base and instruct stages.
No comparison of refusal-training approaches or timing.
